title: KV cache coherence sprint - postmortem and immediate runbook notes
summary: During a planned coherence-sprint rollout for multi-region KV prefix syncing we observed a rapid eviction cascade that produced a region-level latency storm and intermittent 5xxs for streaming sessions. This doc records the timeline, immediate mitigations, root cause analysis hypothesis, and actionable follow-ups including runbook changes and quick fixes to avoid recurrence.
impact: Clients experienced elevated tail latency (p95 -> 4.8s, p99 -> 12.3s) for generation and streaming endpoints for ~42 minutes in eu-west and us-west regions. ~18% of streaming sessions saw chunk reordering or fragmentation; API error rate rose to 2.6% (5xx). No data loss; customer-facing errors were transient but user-visible. SLA thresholds breached for latency-based SLA for 42 minutes.
detection: Pager triggered by SLO-oncall at 02:09 UTC via latency alert (route: /v1/generate p99 token latency). Distributed tracing showed repeated KV cache miss storms and lock contention traces originating from kv-coherence worker group. First human confirmation at 02:12 UTC by oncall.
timeline:
02:05 - Gradual internal rollout of KV-coherence repair job started (deploy GH-PR-5123 to kv-sync service)
02:07 - Metrics show initial uptick in KV eviction rate in eu-west (eviction/sec *3x)
02:09 - Latency alert fires (p99 token latency elevated)
02:10 - Streaming clients report fragmentation; streaming error rate rising
02:12 - Oncall joins, escalates to SRE lead; begin tracing to kv-sync worker
02:14 - Observed lock wait times increasing in kv-sync; concurrent workers retrying prefix syncs
02:18 - Emergency rollback of kv-sync deploy initiated (rollback windowed)
02:21 - Rollback complete; eviction rate stops rising but backlog of pending syncs keeps latency elevated
02:28 - Backpressure queues drained partially; streaming fragmentation rate dropping
02:49 - Metrics return near-baseline; alerts auto-resolve at 02:52
03:00 - Incident declared resolved; post-incident data collection and logs preserved
root_cause: Primary: A coordination change in the kv-coherence repair job introduced optimistic parallel prefix syncs without sufficient leader election gating. Under the typical prefix distribution, rare overlapping prefixes caused repeated cache invalidation and synchronous rehydration across worker processes, producing high KV store read amplification and long lock hold times. Secondary: A TTL misalignment between region-local caches meant entries expired at slightly different times, increasing simultaneous re-fetches after the deploy. Tertiary: The new worker had a higher default retry/backoff aggressiveness (config drift from staging) which amplified contention under load.
mitigation: Immediate actions taken: rolled back kv-sync deploy (02:18), increased local cache TTL from 30s->90s in eu-west/us-west as temporary buffer, disabled parallel sync path (feature-flag off) to stop optimistic simultaneous rehydration. We also temporarily limited worker concurrency for kv-sync to 2 threads per pod to reduce lock contention. These measures returned system to baseline within ~40 minutes.
postmortem_notes:
- The change passed unit/integration tests but did not have a production staging gate that reproduced regional TTL skew.
- Observability gaps: we lacked a specific metric for "prefix-coherence-retries" and per-prefix lock-hold-time histograms which would have surfaced the issue sooner.
- Runbook gap: no explicit rollback step for kv-sync feature gating; immediate rollback was manual and slow because the runbook assumed a single global toggle.
- Communication: Customer success and trust teams were notified at 02:30 and provided a short incident summary; we should automate initial notify for P0s.

metrics: Baseline p99 token latency (pre-incident): 280ms. Peak p99 during incident: 12.3s. API 5xx baseline: 0.04% -> peak 2.6%. KV eviction rate baseline eu-west: 125 evict/s -> peak 420 evict/s. KV-coherence retries observed: ~18k retries during incident window. Streaming fragmentation rate baseline <0.2% -> peak 18%.
runbook_updates:
1) New emergency rollback snippet: 'kubectl set env deployment/kv-sync COHERENCE_PARALLEL=false' and pipeline rollback playbook added.
2) Add step to throttle kv-sync concurrency via config map and provide kubectl commands for quick change.
3) Include clear detection markers: 'coherence.retries > 1000/min' and 'prefix-lock-hold-time p99 > 300ms' to auto-escalate to P0.
4) Add doc section for TTL alignment test cases and staging matrix for multi-region behavior.
communication: Initial page and Slack thread contained technical summary; customer-success notified via email at 02:30 with incident stub. Post-incident: draft customer-facing blurb prepared and routed to legal/comm for sign-off. Internal retro scheduled 2027-12-20 15:00 UTC.
appendix: Observability artifacts attached: exported flamegraphs (s3://redwood-internal/incident-20271216/flamegraphs/), kv-sync logs (s3://redwood-internal/incident-20271216/logs/), and trace snapshots (trace-id: 4b8f2a7c). Raw alert history included. A short reproduction harness is in GH-PR-5123 (tests/integration/kv_coherence_skew_test.py).
notes_to_self: Follow-up: validate that increasing TTL to 90s does not mask other correctness issues. If leader-election gating added, measure end-to-end latency overhead and document expected cost. Consider adding a read-only fallback path that serves slightly stale prefixes instead of blocking rehydration under high contention.
